cards.title: Inject custom Liquid sections into a Shopify theme via Edit Code
cards.summary: Click path for creating a reusable custom section file in a Shopify theme by pasting external HTML/Liquid through the Edit Code interface.
cards.use_when: You need a custom PDP, landing page, or storefront section (founder block, ingredient panel, size chart) that Shopify's default page builder sections cannot produce, and want it reusable across templates.
steps: From the Shopify admin go to Online Store, then open the Themes page.
Find the active theme, click the actions menu, and choose Edit Code to open the code editor.
In the left file tree, open the Sections folder.
Use Add a new section, give the file a descriptive name that ends in .liquid (for example wle_hair_nectar_gg.liquid), and create it.
Paste your prepared HTML/Liquid code into the new file and Save.
The section now appears in the theme customizer's Add Section picker, where you can place it and edit its schema settings.
To update the section later, reopen Edit Code, paste the new code over the old, Save, and hard-refresh the live page to confirm the change rendered.
caveats: Sections live inside the theme, so changes are lost or overwritten if the theme is replaced or updated without carrying the file forward — keep a copy of the Liquid code outside Shopify.
Shopify's Edit Code interface labels and menu positions change; verify the current click path in your admin before following these steps literally.

cards.title: Assign a product to a custom page template
cards.summary: Click path for building a custom Shopify product template that hides default sections and populates your custom Liquid section with a specific product.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a hero or specialty product on a bespoke PDP layout, or building a landing page where you want your custom section to render that product's data.
steps: Create the product first: Products, Add product, upload the images you want the custom section to display, and set the price.
Open Online Store, then Customize Theme to enter the theme editor.
In the template selector at the top, create a new template for the product (for example name it hair_nectar_gg) rather than editing the default product template.
Hide or remove the default sections so only your intended layout shows.
Use Add Section and select the custom Liquid file you created (for example wle_hair_nectar_gg) to place it on the template.
Assign the specific product to the template so the custom section's product object references it and populates correctly.
Preview the template with that product assigned to confirm images, price and section content all render.
caveats: A custom product template only applies to products you assign to it; leaving a product on the default template means the custom layout will not appear.
If the custom section references product objects, it will render empty or broken on products that have no such data assigned.

cards.title: Make a product buyable with inventory set before launch
cards.summary: Ensuring a freshly added Shopify product can actually be added to cart by editing the product and setting available inventory.
cards.use_when: After adding a product through Products, Add product, before driving any traffic — you need to confirm the product is not showing as sold out or unavailable at checkout.
steps: Go to Products in the Shopify admin and open the product you just added.
Set the price and make sure the product is set to Active so it is published to the storefront.
Set available inventory for the variant (the source example uses 10,000 units) and Save.
Open the live storefront product page in a fresh session and confirm the add-to-cart button is enabled rather than showing Sold out.
Add the product to cart and reach the checkout start to verify it is genuinely purchasable end to end.
caveats: The 10,000 figure is just an example from the source, not a recommended stock level — set inventory to match your real replenishment plan.
Inventory can be tracked or untracked per variant; a product with inventory tracking on and zero available will display as sold out even if the page looks correct.

cards.title: Verify each store-setup step on the live storefront
cards.summary: Adding a verification step after every mechanical store configuration task so a click path that 'looked done' is proven to actually work.
cards.use_when: Any time you complete a store setup task — theme code, product, payment, shipping profile or tax — before moving to the next setup item.
steps: After each setup task, define the observable behaviour that proves it worked (product adds to cart, page shows the new section, order can complete).
Open the live storefront in a private/incognito window or offline-test mode so admin-session caching does not mask problems.
Exercise the exact customer action tied to that task — add to cart, reach checkout, submit a test order where your payment settings allow it.
If you edited Liquid, hard-refresh the live page rather than trusting the theme editor preview, which can show unsaved or cached states.
Record the setup item as verified only after the live behaviour matches, then move on.
caveats: Preferences and interfaces vary; the specific test steps depend on your payment, shipping and tax configuration, so adapt the verification to each item.
Test orders and payment gateways may need test mode or refunding, which is outside the scope of the pure click path.

05-SET / store and domain setup

Goes here. Going from nothing to a live store. Domain and email, store configuration, payments and tax, shipping profiles, tracking install, legal pages, and the verification step that proves each one actually worked. Specifically capturing the mechanical click paths for importing external HTML/Liquid code into a Shopify theme via the "Edit Code" interface to create custom sections, and adding physical products to populate those custom Liquid templates.

Not here.

AI image generation prompts and brand board creation -> 04-BRD

Supplier sourcing and margin calculation -> 18-COG

Product research and competitive validation -> 01-PRD

Landing page section strategy (e.g., adding "us vs them" or founder blocks) -> 07-LPG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Provides the exact click path for importing external HTML/Liquid code into a Shopify theme's backend to create custom, reusable page sections without using Shopify's default page builder. modules: [SET] topics: [store configuration] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. store configuration.

Look for. The exact click path to inject custom Liquid code into a Shopify theme: Online Store -> Edit Code -> Sections -> Add a new Section -> Name the file (e.g., wle_hair_nectar_gg.liquid) -> Paste HTML/Liquid code -> Save. The exact click path to assign a product to a custom page template: Products -> Add product -> Upload images and set price -> Online Store -> Customize Theme -> Create a new template (e.g., hair_nectar_gg) -> Hide default sections -> Add Section -> Select the custom Liquid file created earlier -> Assign the specific product to populate the section. The exact click path to ensure a product is buyable: Products -> Edit product -> Set Available inventory (e.g., 10,000) -> Save. The process for updating existing custom code: Edit Code -> Paste new code over old code -> Save -> Refresh live page.

Skip. General marketing advice, AI tool promotion (e.g., "White Labeler AI Vault," "Top View," "Claude Design"), branding theory, and dropshipping vs. private labeling strategies. Anything not directly related to the mechanical click paths within the Shopify admin interface.

Scope mix. Nearly all baseline.

Volume. 10 to 15.
